manifest.description: Opens STL, OBJ and PLY meshes as editable designs: recognises plates, holes and fillets and rebuilds them as a parametric history; anything not recognised is kept as a mesh. Project: https://github.com/stritti/revmesh
manifest.stl.units.title: Units
manifest.stl.units.description: Mesh files are unitless and assumed to be mm; inch: the file is read as inches and converted to millimetres
progress.checking: Checking the design in the app's sandbox
report.smoothed.title: Facets smoothed
report.smoothed.message: Holes and rounded corners are rebuilt as true circles, so the volume changes by {change}% from the mesh's facets.
report.deviation.title: Surface deviation per face
report.deviation.message: The mesh's faces lie at most this far from the recognised faces: {faces}.
report.unrecognized.title: Kept as a mesh
report.slanted.title: Kept as a mesh — slanted in the file
report.slanted.message: Recognised as {summary}, but its axis lies slanted in the file: SolidCraft sketches on its origin planes only, so the part is kept as a mesh.
report.units.title: Units converted
report.units.message: The file was read as inches and converted to millimetres.
report.selfcheck.title: The recognised design failed the app's rebuild check
report.selfcheck.message: SolidCraft could not open or rebuild it: {reason}. The file is kept as a mesh body instead.
report.too_large.title: Too large to recognise
report.too_large.message: The mesh has {triangles} triangles; recognising more than {max} would exceed the memory budget, so it is kept exactly as it is.
report.update.title: A newer version of revmesh is available
report.update.message: This import ran with revmesh {current}, but {latest} is out. Install it from https://github.com/stritti/revmesh/releases
summary.stack: A {x} x {y} x {z} mm part of {n} outlines stacked along {axis}
summary.chamfer: a {w} x {h} mm chamfer on its top
summary.combined: A {x} x {y} x {z} mm part of outlines extruded along {axes}
stl.too_short: the file is too short to be an STL file
stl.truncated: the binary STL header announces {expected} triangles, but the file has only {actual} bytes
stl.syntax.reason.ends_inside_solid: the file ends inside a solid or facet
stl.syntax.reason.too_many_vertices: a facet already has three vertices
stl.syntax.reason.facet_vertex_count: a facet has three vertices, this one has {n}
stl.non_finite: triangle {triangle} has a corner that is not a finite number (nan or inf)
stl.out_of_range: triangle {triangle} has a coordinate too large for an STL mesh (beyond about 3.4e38)
stl.size_limit: the STL is {size} bytes; this import supports at most {max_bytes} bytes
stl.allocation: there is not enough memory to hold the STL triangles
mesh.size_limit: the file is {size} bytes; this import supports at most {max_bytes} bytes
mesh.non_finite: triangle {triangle} has a corner that is not a finite number (nan or inf)
mesh.out_of_range: triangle {triangle} has a coordinate too large for a mesh (beyond about 3.4e38)
mesh.allocation: there is not enough memory to hold the mesh triangles
obj.syntax.reason.vertex_not_three: a vertex line needs at least three coordinates
obj.syntax.reason.index_out_of_range: vertex index {n} is out of range
obj.syntax.reason.face_too_small: a face has fewer than three corners, this one has {n}
ply.reason.unsupported_format: unsupported PLY format {format}; ascii 1.0 and binary_little_endian 1.0 are read
ply.reason.missing_vertex: the header has no vertex element
ply.reason.no_vertex_coords: the vertex element has no x, y and z coordinates
ply.reason.missing_face: the header has no face element
ply.reason.no_face_list: the face element has no vertex index list
ply.reason.truncated: the file ends before all records are read
ply.reason.index_out_of_range: vertex index {n} is out of range
ply.reason.face_too_small: a face has fewer than three corners, this one has {n}
ply.reason.line_too_long: a line is longer than 4 MiB
